question: Which of the following was enacted in 1860 in British India?
solution:
The correct answer is **Indian Penal Code**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indian Penal Code (IPC)** was enacted in 1860.
 
• The IPC is the comprehensive code intended to cover all substantive aspects of criminal law in India.
 
• It was drafted by the first law commission under the chairmanship of **Lord Macaulay**.
 
• The IPC has been amended several times to incorporate new laws and regulations.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
 

 Option
 Details
 
 

 Option 1: The Permanent Settlement of Bengal
 Introduced in 1793 by Lord Cornwallis, it was an agreement between the East India Company and Bengali landlords to fix revenues.
 
 

 Option 2: Hindu Widow's Remarriage Act
 Enacted in 1856, it legalized the remarriage of Hindu widows in British India.
 
 

 Option 3: Indian Penal Code
 Enacted in 1860, it is the main criminal code of India, covering all substantive aspects of criminal law.
 
 

 Option 4: Indian Evidence Act
 Enacted in 1872, it sets the rules and procedures regarding admissibility of evidence in Indian courts.
